goal: Stand up our governance starter kit: a judge for answer faithfulness, an eval dataset to score against, and a review queue for human checks.

expected_steps.interaction: input form (Aria needs information): enter name, instructions, feedback value type and tags from judges/answer-faithfulness.judge.json, then Approve
input form: enter name, description and questions from review-queues/governance-review.queue.json, then Approve
input form: enter name, description and tags from datasets/release-candidates.dataset.json, then Approve
SKIP this step (Skip step on its form): there are no traces to enqueue yet. It is proposed only because it shares the 'review queue' domain. Its queue_id is wired from review_queue.create.

notes: Steps run in registry order (judge, review queue, test set, enqueue), not the order of the sentence. Each step asks for its own name: the planner only wires a field that points at an earlier step's result, here review_queue.add_items.queue_id <- review_queue.create. Under autonomy=ask_each every step raises an input form and then an Approve/Deny prompt; under approve_plan and auto_guarded only the input forms appear.
